explanation: Amsterdam is where the Schengen acquis was taken into Union law, and the agreement’s own history says the negotiations were the same ones. The article reads: "It was during those negotiations, which led to the Amsterdam Treaty, that the incorporation of the Schengen acquis into the main body of European Union law was agreed along with opt-outs for Ireland and the United Kingdom (which subsequently withdrew from the EU in 2020), which were to remain outside of the Schengen Area."
